note: Curated pointed forms and phrases used by lessons, added 2026-11-10. These lemmas were missing from the generated vocabulary or needed as whole phrases. Not a clergy review. Do not treat as generated data.

entries.reason: The noun 'map' is מַפָּה. Lesson I-40 had been using מִפָּה, which is a verb form 'to map'.

entries.en: a charger (for a phone or battery)
entries.reason: An electrical charger is מַטְעֵן. Lesson I-16 had been using מִטְעָן, which means cargo or a charge (load).

entries.en: a course (a class or series of classes)
entries.reason: An academic course is קוּרְס. Lesson I-37 had been using קוֹרֵס, which means 'is collapsing'.
Israeli Hebrew sense used in lesson I-18; the generated lexicon had no reserve-duty entry.

entries.en: a good final sealing (Yom Kippur greeting)
entries.reason: The usual Yom Kippur greeting, distinct from שָׁנָה טוֹבָה on Rosh Hashana.

entries.en: a kosher and happy holiday (Pesach greeting)
entries.reason: The common Pesach greeting; חַג שָׂמֵחַ alone is also used.

entries.en: take care of yourself (said to a woman)
entries.reason: Feminine counterpart of תִּשְׁמֹר עַל עַצְמְךָ.
